label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
which_first: 03, because it is short enough for a phone between other things and still ends on four steps I could do tonight.

03.one_line: Quick, a story with a clock, a hold and a 6 pm stop, then four steps small enough to take tonight; I got it without knowing any code.

10.one_line: Same factory with the fights and the failures left in, which makes it feel real, but the steps are on page 11 and I would have drifted before then.

tomorrow: Open the AI agent tool I already use for my app, make a new empty project with nothing private in it, and write a half-page of rules for one agent: what it is for, what it may change, when it must stop and ask. Then a one-line brief ('a page answering what my users ask most, by Friday') and see what it ships by evening.
would_share: yes, with the two friends who build apps with me; I would send edition 03 page 5, the four steps, because it is the one page they can act on tonight.
why_buy: Each step would need a worked example from an app like mine, a 'do this now' I can finish in an evening, and the failures kept in. A real cost line for a student budget would seal it.

best_page.why: The stop at 18:44 lands, then the four numbered steps are concrete, small and say what to keep out (no passwords, no keys). It is the page that answers 'can I do this'.

worst_page.why: A list of file paths and a letter number (claims/register.json, C101, briefs/...) is exactly the repo-speak that loses me; the 'why this page is here' idea is good but the sources block reads as insider noise.

one_change_before_the_editor_sees_it: Edition 10, page 3: replace the 'Figure to come' box (and the other placeholders on pages 4, 8, 9) with the real picture, or cut the box, because the dashed 'to come' frames make a phone read feel unfinished; and move 'start now' to the top of page 3, since the pointer on page 4 comes too late.
notes: The cover and the little characters are the best thing: they make it feel like my kind of book, not a manual. Page-end 'Dramatised. Rests on...' lines and codes like C101, C037, C088, R5 are jargon I skipped. The small agent icons are tiny on a phone. $20 a month is the first number I would check and it is easy to find, which I liked; a free route is mentioned but thin. The first factory scene in 03 is dense for a first page, with five speakers before any glossary, though the grey 'Words on this page' boxes rescued it.
